claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Birkelunden is a named 16.3-decare public park bounded by Seilduksgata, Toftes gate/Grünerløkka school, Schleppegrells gate and Thorvald Meyers gate, with Paulus' plass and Paulus church adjacent to the west.
claims.inference_limit: The 16.3-decare area is the park, not the ca. 116-decare protected cultural environment.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Birkelunden was laid out by Thorvald Meyer in the 1860s as part of his planning and subdivision of Grünerløkka.
claims.inference_limit: Do not restamp wider Grünerløkka development history as if every detail occurred inside the park.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Thorvald Meyer transferred Birkelunden free of charge to the municipal planting authority in 1882.
claims.inference_limit: The transfer supports a direct Meyer–park relation, not unrelated biographical claims.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The 1882 gift was made on the condition that the park should never be built on.
claims.inference_limit: Do not expand this into a claim about every later planning decision without additional evidence.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The planting was redesigned and renewed in 1916–1920 to create a practical children's play area with play equipment and access for an ice rink.
claims.inference_limit: Useful for history/before-after research; image publication rights remain separate.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The present music pavilion was built in 1926 to a design by architect Otto Hald after an architectural competition.
claims.inference_limit: Object ID, ownership and image/provenance must be audited before materializing an Object.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: A water basin was constructed in Birkelunden in 1927–1928.
claims.inference_limit: Present physical condition/use should be checked separately if described as current.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The park was called Birkelunden from the start, was officially rendered Bjerkelunden in 1926, and changed back to Birkelunden in 1955.
claims.inference_limit: This is a real language/name-history candidate; broader etymology requires separate language-source review.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Ørnulf Bast's bronze sculpture Føll was erected in Birkelunden in 1953.
claims.inference_limit: Object materialization still requires canonical ID, ownership and asset review.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Jack Johnsen's pensioner organizing began among 10–12 pensioners meeting on a bench in Birkelunden; in 1937 a group of 18 established Venner i Bjerkelunden.
claims.inference_limit: Do not publish an oldest-association superlative without independent corroboration.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: A bust of Jack Johnsen was erected in Birkelunden by pensioners in 1984.
claims.inference_limit: The bust is an Object candidate; image/license and canonical ownership are separate gates.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Birkelunden received new park works including basin and planting improvements in 1984–1986.
claims.inference_limit: Potential before/after/change claim; historical-image rights remain separate.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Nils Aas made the Birkelunden memorial to Norwegians who fought with the International Brigades in the Spanish Civil War; it was erected in 1989.
claims.inference_limit: SNL currently gives 1889; that conflicting date is rejected against Oslo byleksikon and Nils Aas Kunstverksted. Preserve the conflict note.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Birkelunden park is one component of the protected Birkelunden cultural environment, which covers about 116 decares and also includes Grünerløkka school, Paulus church and 15 blocks with 139 tenements.
claims.inference_limit: The 116 decares, blocks and buildings belong to the cultural environment and must never be used as the park's own area or structure inventory.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The protection process for Birkelunden cultural environment began in 1996 and the cultural environment was protected on 28 April 2006.
claims.inference_limit: This describes the larger cultural environment; wording must keep that scope explicit.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Oslo municipality currently lists a pavilion with power outlets and drinking fountains as Birkelunden facilities.
claims.inference_limit: Reverify before future onsite/current-use publication; facility presence does not prove event schedules.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Thorvald Meyer developed the Grünerløkka property and laid out Birkelunden as a park before transferring it to the municipality without payment.
claims.inference_limit: Use People-owned evidence for wider biography; this relation is place-specific.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Oslo municipality's park-history feature identifies Birkelunden as a site of labour-movement mass gatherings in the early 1900s.
claims.locator: Historisk fakta om parkene i Oslo
claims.inference_limit: Suitable as historical-use evidence but not yet a Story: episode-specific date, protagonists and narrative axis are still required.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: OpenStreetMap way 3236549 is the named park geometry already accepted in Birkelunden coordinate evidence.
claims.inference_limit: Geometry evidence only; no historical inference.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Birkelunden, Olaf Ryes plass and Schous plass are separate parks/places along Thorvald Meyers gate on Grünerløkka.
claims.inference_limit: Shared geography does not transfer people, objects, stories, brands or place-authored prose between the parks.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Olaf Ryes plass is a named square/park bounded by Markveien, Grüners gate, Thorvald Meyers gate and Sofienberggata.
claims.inference_limit: Downstream seed only; does not approve Olaf Ryes plass production.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The area that became Olaf Ryes plass was part of an open lot bought by the municipality in 1863, regulated as a square and named Olaf Ryes plass in 1864.
claims.inference_limit: Downstream seed; Olaf Rye biography beyond the naming relation belongs to People-owned evidence.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Olaf Ryes plass was developed as a park in 1890.
claims.inference_limit: Downstream seed only.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: A bronze bust of Eilert Sundt by Mathias Skeibrok was erected at the south end of Olaf Ryes plass in 1892.
claims.inference_limit: Downstream Object seed; canonical ID/asset/provenance remain open.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: A centrally placed fountain was installed at Olaf Ryes plass in 1927.
claims.inference_limit: Downstream Object seed; current condition/function should be reverified.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Oslo municipality currently lists a fountain and power outlet as facilities at Olaf Ryes plass.
claims.inference_limit: Downstream seed; reverify when Olaf Ryes reaches current/onsite production.
